rules.title: Rules
rules.intro: Build compound verbs as lines of cards on the table. The first to empty their hand wins. On your turn, make one of these plays:
rules.lineBody: A meaning card from your hand, a verb from the table or your hand, and every particle it needs from the tops of the river. A wildcard stands in for any particle.
rules.crossBody: Lay your verb from your hand on one side of a particle already down and your meaning on the other. It gets a crossing mark.
rules.loneBody: Lay one verb on the table, then draw 2 cards. Not allowed once the deck and the meaning pile are both empty.
rules.swapBody: Swap a meaning card from your hand for the face-up one. Yours goes to the bottom of the meaning pile and the next card turns face up. In turns, a swap uses your turn and counts like a pass towards turning the river. With answers shown, the face-up card lights when it would make a line for you now.
rules.passBody: In turns, you can always draw a card and pass instead; when everyone has passed or swapped in a row, each river pile turns its top card under. In a race, tap Stuck when you can't play; when nobody can play, everyone draws 1 and each river pile turns its top card under.
rules.endBody: Empty your hand first to win. Once the deck is empty, two stalls in a row with no line laid end the game, and the fewest cards wins; so do four stalls in a row with nothing laid at all. Equal fewest share the win.
rules.cardsBody: Verbs are gorse, with notches on all four sides. Adverbs are deep heather with square notches; prepositions pale heather with round ones. Wildcards have a dashed edge. Meaning cards show three English meanings and their Irish.
rules.symbolsBody: A few marks on the table's cards. Tap any card on the table to see it in full.
rules.sym.glyphs: Zoomed far out, each card shows only its type: verb, adverb, preposition, wildcard, meaning.
rules.sym.cross: A line crosses through this particle.
rules.sym.owner: Who laid the card, in their seat colour.
rules.sym.arrive: The meaning shown belongs to the line that comes in on the marked side.
rules.sym.split: Two meanings in use: each half sits against the side its line comes in on, the second in reverse colours.
rules.sym.multi: Three or four meanings in use, with the count. Tap it to read them.
rules.sym.peek: Tapped open: every meaning in use is marked, with an arrow for the way its line runs into the card (from the left, →). [1/2] means the same Irish has another meaning in the deck.
rules.modesBody: Turns: one play each, at your own pace. Race: everyone plays at once, and a play is checked the moment you lay it. If someone took a card you needed first, your line is cleared and you lose nothing. Race depends on speed; turns are an equal game.
rules.hiddenBody: Meaning cards show only the English and nothing lights up. Build the line yourself; it is checked when you lay it. A wrong line costs your turn, or a 3-second wait in a race.
settings.title: Settings
settings.creditsBody: Game and rules by Phil. Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque and Atkinson Hyperlegible, both under the SIL Open Font License. Works offline; nothing leaves this device.
tut.1.title: These are meaning cards
tut.1.body: Each one has three English meanings, with the Irish under each. Tap the card with DESCRIBE.
tut.2.title: This is the river
tut.2.body: Particles come only from here, never from your hand. You can take the top card of any pile. Tap síos.
tut.3.title: Now the verb
tut.3.body: cuir síos ar needs cuir. There is one on the table. Tap it, and the line lays itself.
tut.4.title: Where it goes
tut.4.body: Lines go at the best free spot. To choose the spot yourself, press and hold the last card instead of tapping.
tut.5.title: {name}'s turn
tut.5.body: Bots play the same way. Watch the line draw in.
tut.6.title: When you can't play
tut.6.body: Draw and pass is always allowed. When everyone passes in a row, every river pile turns its top card under. Tap Draw and pass.
tut.7.title: Swapping a meaning card
tut.7.body: No line for your meanings? Tap one of your meaning cards, then this face-up one, to swap them. A swap uses your turn and counts like a pass towards turning the river.
tut.8.title: Wildcards
tut.8.body: A wildcard stands in for any particle the river can't give you. It's only spent when you tap it, so you choose when. Once laid it stays on the table as that particle, so each wildcard is used once.
tut.9.title: More ways to make a line
tut.9.body: A line can end on a meaning card already on the table, as any of its three meanings: tap one to see them. A line that uses nothing on the table draws you 2 cards, so build off what's there.
tut.end.title: You're ready
tut.end.body: Play the rest of this game. Empty your hand first to win.

rules.sfBody: A Stórfhocal is a word tile that completes a set phrase, such as aire in tabhair aire do. Laid in its place in the phrase, it makes a line with no meaning card: the verb, then the phrase's particles from the river (or a wildcard, or a particle already down), with the tile where the phrase puts it. Nothing runs through a tile. Hard bots now and then lay one. Take one of yours from the bag with the Stórfhocail button: one at a time, free to put back, and it never counts as a card in your hand.
rules.sfStakesBody: Nothing is at stake until a tile is laid. Win outright and you keep every tile on the table: yours stay in your bag and a bot's join it. Lose to a bot and the tiles you laid leave your bag for good; a bot's tiles leave the game. On a shared win each side keeps its own. Restarting, discarding, or starting a new game over a saved one counts as losing. Nothing ventured, nothing gained: while you hold tiles but none of yours is waiting for an answer, Hard bots rarely lay one. Lay one and their odds are back to normal until a bot lays one in reply. With nothing in your bag they play at normal odds.
